quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What can help reduce the chances of a collision?

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not on your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers. This reduces your risk of being hit. Always watch what other drivers are doing around you.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, squeeze both the front and rear brakes at the same time with controlled pressure.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket, what should it do?

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket made of leather or another tough material. It should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
It can be a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see everything you need to ride safely.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other substances?

options.text: It is absorbed very quickly into the bloodstream.
It must be digested before entering the bloodstream.
It can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is absorbed very quickly into the bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream and reaches the brain quickly.

questions.question: What can help reduce the chances of a crash?
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready to respond to changes.

questions.question: When riding at night, is it easier or harder to judge distances?

options.text: About the same as during the day.

questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Light and shadows help you see how far away things are. At night, headlights may distort or hide these cues.

questions.question: Can motorcyclists use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes?
questions.explanation: In Tennessee, motorcyclists are allowed to use HOV lanes any time, regardless of how many riders are on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding?

options.text: Yes, to keep your hands warm.
Yes, they improve grip and protect your hands.
No, they can interfere with the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they improve grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: A protective jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.explanation: Your riding jacket should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement. This balance keeps you safe and comfortable.

questions.question: When scanning around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
See if you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, or schools.
questions.explanation: Look for escape routes in intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones. This helps you identify safe options if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign shows that U-turns are not allowed in this area. Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as on your motorcycle.
Immediately take it on the highway.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle on the road, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe, controlled area.

questions.question: There is less traction for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, less traction is available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do so carefully.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen in daylight, you should:

options.text: Not wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Bright clothing makes you easier to see, so wear it whenever you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: What are the best colors for motorcycle riders to wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green are the best colors for riders. These colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols and warn drivers about road conditions. This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: How can you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will help you sober up. Your body needs time to remove the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, and other methods do not speed this process.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Pick a lane position that helps you avoid hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: A good lane position should:

options.text: Help you see others and let them see you.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and let them see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good position also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you room to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked often by all riders.
Be used only by the lead rider.
Not be checked often because they distract you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked often by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often. This helps you watch the riders behind you and makes sure the group stays together.

questions.question: Motorcycle mirrors:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass you. Speeding up may only cause them to tailgate at the higher speed, which is even more dangerous.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection without traffic lights at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic lights or signs, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be as visible as possible when riding, even during the day. Reflective clothing is also helpful.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire affects steering, which affects your balance.
A flat front tire disables the front brake.
A flat front tire prevents you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering hard. This hurts your ability to balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: When riding, wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Riding shoes should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on surfaces. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.
